regime_context: The detector reads as a broad, two-hub resource narrative concentrated in Oil & Gas Producers (strong rank + high breadth + crowded, but mixed trend-health) and Gold Miners (second rank, low breadth, non-crowded). Eight of sixteen themes are eligible, and the absolute-trend gate has historically helped on this market, so the discipline is worth honoring — but the rotating leader/challenger margin is narrow by construction and the rotation read is display-only.
emerging_watch: Watching whether Gold Miners close the score gap on Oil & Gas Producers while maintaining its non-crowded profile — a condition that would confirm a genuine two-pillar resource regime rather than a fading single leader. I retire this watch if XGD.TO's breadth (currently 0.267) does not rise above 0.4 within the next 15 trading days.

theses.subject: Oil & Gas Producers
theses.thesis: The theme holds the top momentum rank, the strongest durability bar (0.68), and the broadest breadth (0.786) — a coherent, broadly-participating leader rather than a one-name squeeze. The absolute-trend gate is the one validated leg and it is currently eligible, so the theme survives the discipline's drawdown filter. Crowding (z=1.04) is flagged only as a size-down caution, not a fade.
theses.dissent: Energy leadership is reflexively crowded and the headline breadth may be inflated by the whole sector moving with crude; a sharp WTI reversal would hit this theme hardest precisely because everyone is positioned there.

falsifier.text: XEG.TO closes below its 50-day average while SPX/TSX itself is unchanged or higher over a 10-day window

theses.subject: Gold Miners
theses.thesis: Gold Miners are the rotation challenger (rank 2, score 1.11) with a non-crowded profile (z=0.2) and eligible status under the trend gate. The durable, non-crowded runner-up setup is the kind of breadth-confirmed second theme the discipline can hold alongside the leader without triggering the 'one-narrative' reflexivity warning.
evidence: rank=2, challenger in rotation with score 1.11
theses.dissent: Breadth is very low (0.267) — this may be a narrow, large-cap-driven move rather than genuine sector participation, and a mean-reverting quality (hurst_tag=mixed) argues against staying power.

falsifier.text: XGD.TO lags XEG.TO by more than 4% over a rolling 10-day window

theses.subject: Big Banks
theses.thesis: Big Banks carry a clean 'trend' hurst tag and a respectable durability bar (0.59) with no crowding (z=-0.01), and they remain eligible under the absolute-trend gate. The financials leg is the quiet, non-crowded trend alternative to the resource-heavy top of the book.
evidence: hurst_tag='trend' (only high-ranked theme with clean trend tag besides Pipelines)
theses.dissent: The momentum score is only 0.423 — fifth rank and a full point below the leader — and the theme offers no catalyst of its own; it is a defensive default, not a leadership read.

falsifier.text: ZEB.TO breaks below its 50-day average while Oil & Gas producers remain above theirs

macro_narrative.note: market-level macro/policy/geo narrative flow; coincident, not per-theme, never a trigger
